# Catalog Clause

Describes one offer and one supplier's catalog, and creates immutable quotes from selected items. Optional `parameters.offer.title`, `text` and `sections` provide authored descriptive content. They create no booking, date, availability or payment requirements; executable date requirements come from catalog items.

## Catalog and bindings

`bindings.state` points to the catalog, defaulting to `/catalog`; `bindings.quotes` points to keyed quote snapshots, defaulting to `/quotes`. Overrides relocate these reads and writes within the executing document. Both bindings must be non-root JSON pointers. These defaults specify locations, not initial data.

The catalog requires exactly `revision`, `supplierId`, `currency` and `entries`. `revision` is an integer from 1 to 1,000,000. `currency` is three-character text; validation does not establish that it is a recognized currency code. `entries` is a dictionary of 1–100 items keyed by item identifier.

Each item requires:

- `label`: 1–120 characters.
- `pricingUnit`: `per_unit` or `per_selected_hour`.
- `dateRequired`: Boolean controlling whether a selection must supply `serviceDate`.
- `maxQuantity`: integer from 1 to 1,000, limiting each selected line's quantity.
- `unitAmountMinor`: integer from 0 to 100,000,000, in the catalog's currency minor units.

Optional `description` is 1–2,000 characters. Optional `guestDiscountPercent` is an integer from 0 to 100; pricing treats omission as zero and applies it without a separate buyer eligibility check. `dateSelectionHint` is descriptive text of 1–500 characters, allowed only when `dateRequired` is true. For `per_unit`, `allowedDurationHours` must be absent or empty. For `per_selected_hour`, it must contain 1–24 distinct integer choices, each from 1 to 168 hours.

Supplier identifiers, item identifiers and quote keys are 1–64 characters, contain neither `/` nor `~`, and cannot start with `$`. They cannot equal `name`, `description`, `type`, `itemType`, `keyType`, `valueType`, `value`, `items`, `blueId`, `blue`, `schema`, `constraints`, `mergePolicy`, `properties` or `contracts`. Catalog, item, publication, quote and selection objects reject unsupported fields.

## Actions and outcomes

`validate` runs automatically once on `initialized`. It validates the existing catalog and requires `quotes`, if present, to be an empty object. It returns `acceptedNew` without creating catalog or quote data. Missing state is otherwise unknown, not an implied initialized value.

`publish` requires exactly `expectedRevision` and `entries`. The expected revision must match the current revision, which must be below 1,000,000. After validating all replacement entries, it replaces the complete item dictionary and increments `revision`, preserving `supplierId` and `currency`. It returns `acceptedNew` with the new revision and emits `Catalog Published` with `clause` and `revision`. A stale revision, invalid entries or the revision ceiling rejects publication. Existing quote snapshots remain unchanged.

`quote` requires exactly `key`, `catalogRevision` and `lines`. For an existing key, an exactly equal stored `intent` returns `duplicate` without rewriting the snapshot or emitting another quote event; any different intent fails with `QUOTE_KEY_CONFLICT`. This duplicate check precedes capacity, revision and pricing checks, so an exact retry can remain a duplicate after the catalog changes. A new quote requires fewer than 200 stored quotes and a `catalogRevision` matching the current catalog.

`lines` must contain 1–20 selections. Each requires `itemId` and integer `quantity` from 1 through that item's `maxQuantity`. Unknown items are rejected. `serviceDate` is required when `dateRequired` is true and forbidden otherwise. It must be a valid `YYYY-MM-DD` calendar date in 2000–2099; this check does not establish availability or require a future date. `durationHours` is required for `per_selected_hour`, must match an offered duration, and is forbidden for `per_unit`. Repeated selections with the same item, service date and duration are rejected even if their quantities differ.

Pricing records `billableUnits` as quantity for `per_unit`, or quantity extended by selected hours for `per_selected_hour`. Each line stores the unit price, pre-discount `subtotalMinor`, applied `guestDiscountPercent`, half-up rounded `discountMinor`, and discounted `lineTotalMinor`. Rounding occurs separately per line. Line and quote pre-discount subtotals cannot exceed 1,000,000,000,000 minor units. Quote `subtotalMinor`, `discountMinor` and `totalMinor` are stored sums of their respective line amounts, all in the snapshot's `currency`.

A new snapshot preserves `intent`, `catalogBlueId`, `catalogRevision`, `supplierId`, `currency`, priced `lines` and totals. Lines preserve `itemId`, `itemLabel`, pricing details and applicable `serviceDate` and `durationHours`, plus `itemDescription` and `dateSelectionHint` when supplied. Creation returns `acceptedNew` with `key` and emits `Quote Created` with `clause`, `quoteKey`, `catalogRevision` and `totalMinor`. These amounts describe a quote, not reserved, secured, captured or paid funds; a selected date is not a confirmed booking.

## Connections

`publish` and `quote` have no default actor or trigger. Named action connections determine invocation sources and `params`; workflow connections require an authenticated `party` or `channel`. A callable action alone grants no viewer permission or personal obligation. Connection `when` can skip execution, and `parameters.conditions` can reject a named action. `before` runs before the action body; `after` and completion of a `once` connection occur only for `acceptedNew`, so a duplicate skips those later steps but can already have run `before`. Invalid catalog operations fail rather than returning a stored rejection status. Changing an installed clause configuration requires a new clause key.

Action invocation is an attempt; accepted effects and stored snapshots establish catalog publication or quote creation, without confirming external fulfillment or payment.
